html:
Pewa is probably the map's misspelling of Tewa, a Pueblo people of the Rio Grande valley north of Santa Fe, New Mexico. They speak a Tanoan language and live in towns such as Ohkay Owingeh, Santa Clara and San Ildefonso.

They farmed maize, beans and squash with irrigation from the river and lived in compact adobe towns. In 1598 Juan de Oñate set up the first Spanish capital of New Mexico beside Ohkay Owingeh. Spanish rule brought tribute, forced labour and attacks on Pueblo religion. In 1680 Popé, a religious leader from Ohkay Owingeh, led the Pueblo Revolt, which drove the Spanish out for twelve years. Some Tewa later moved west to live among the Hopi. San Ildefonso became famous in the 1900s for the black pottery of María Martínez. Their neighbours include the Tano.
